Change c0289. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XV.

Context before (unchanged): Their happiness was not decreased by the absence of summer.

1818 text: They loved, and sympathized with one another; and their joys, depending on each other, were not interrupted by the casualties that took place around them. The more I saw of them, the greater became my desire to claim their protection and kindness; my heart yearned to be known and loved by these amiable creatures: to see their sweet looks turned towards me with affection, was the utmost limit of my ambition.

1831 text: They loved, and sympathised with one another; and their joys, depending on each other, were not interrupted by the casualties that took place around them. The more I saw of them, the greater became my desire to claim their protection and kindness; my heart yearned to be known and loved by these amiable creatures: to see their sweet looks directed towards me with affection, was the utmost limit of my ambition.

The more I saw of them, the greater became my desire to claim their protection and kindness; my heart yearned to be known and loved by these amiable creatures: to see their sweet looks [-turned-] {+directed+} towards me with affection, was the utmost limit of my ambition.

Context after (unchanged): I dared not think that they would turn them from me with disdain and horror.

result.rationale: Two small changes: 'sympathized' becomes 'sympathised' (orthography), and 'turned towards me' becomes 'directed towards me' (synonymous diction). Meaning is unchanged. The 'turn them from me' echo in the following context is slightly weakened.
